commitResults.messageTitle: Add new feature to let the chatbot understand specific dates and times

commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, the startup banner, separators, task rendering, confirmations, and error messages out of Yuki into a dedicated Ui class. Keep command parsing and task mutations in Yuki so this increment stays narrowly scoped and preserves the existing CLI transcript. This establishes the user-interface boundary required by the OOP refactor while leaving Parser and TaskList extraction independent for later iterations.

Move command normalization, command-type recognition, task construction, task-number parsing, and no-argument validation out of Yuki into a stateless Parser utility. Keep task-index range checks in Yuki for now because they depend on the underlying collection and will move naturally with the later TaskList extraction. Simplify CommandType back to an enum that only represents supported commands. Add a portable test-ui plan covering valid commands and parser error paths with exact console-output assertions so future refactors can detect visible regressions.

Introduce TaskList as the owner of Yuki's ordered tasks and move add, delete, lookup, mark, unmark, size, one-based index conversion, and range validation behind its methods. Copy tasks loaded from Storage and expose unmodifiable snapshots for display and persistence so callers cannot mutate the internal collection accidentally. Simplify Yuki to coordinate Parser, TaskList, Storage, and Ui without performing collection operations directly. Update the exact-output UI test descriptions to document the TaskList behavior they protect.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move Yuki lifecycle into an instance
commitResults.messageBody: Give Yuki final Ui, Storage, and TaskList fields so one application object owns the dependencies used throughout a session. Load saved tasks in the constructor, move the command loop into an instance run method, and reduce main to constructing and starting Yuki. Keep command dispatch unchanged in this increment so the lifecycle refactor remains independent from the upcoming Command hierarchy. Update the exact-output test plan to state that it protects the constructor and run flow.

Add an abstract Command contract plus AddCommand, DeleteCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, ListCommand, and ExitCommand implementations that own command-specific execution. Make Parser.parse the single public parsing entry point and return a fully configured Command object after validating user input. Replace Yuki's command-type switch with a small read, parse, execute, and isExit loop so the application controller no longer knows individual command types. Preserve each command's existing display and persistence order, and update the exact-output UI test descriptions for the new dispatch architecture.

commitResults.messageBody:
Bring the Java sources in line with the SE-EDU coding standard so
future changes follow consistent documentation and layout conventions.

- Complete Javadocs and punctuate block-tag descriptions
- Wrap long expressions and use plural names for arrays
- Remove redundant comments and order static imports consistently

Preserve existing parser, task, storage, and CLI behavior.

Define the expected JUnit coverage focus and require relevant tests after
code changes. This keeps future agent work aligned with project quality
requirements.

Require agents to apply the CS2103T Java coding-standard skill before
writing, editing, or reviewing Java code.

Document the precedence, compatibility, verification, and reporting rules
needed to keep future style changes consistent and behavior-preserving.

Require agents to apply the CS2103T Git standard skill when drafting,
reviewing, or creating commits.

Record subject, body, coherence, authorization, and verification rules so
future commits use evidence-based metadata and preserve unrelated work.
